body_text: Firm News 6.3.26 Crescent Capital Group Closes Largest Fund in Firm’s History with Fourth U.S. Direct Lending Fund, Raising $10.8 Billion in Investable Capital CDL IV Represents One of the Largest Lower Middle Market Direct Lending Funds to Date LOS ANGELES, NEW YORK, BOSTON, CHICAGO – June 3, 2026 – Crescent Capital Group LP (“Crescent”), one of the leading alternative credit investment firms, announced today the successful final close of its fourth U.S. direct lending fund, Crescent Direct Lending Fund IV (“CDL Fund IV”), raising $10.8 billion in investable capital, including targeted leverage and separately managed accounts investing alongside the fund. Since inception in 2005, the Crescent Direct Lending team has issued more than $17.0 billion of aggregate loan commitments to more than 285 companies in a variety of industries and over 150 distinct private equity sponsors. title: MediciNova CEO Provides Shareholder Update
summary: LA JOLLA, Calif., June 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- MediciNova, Inc., a biopharmaceutical company traded on the NASDAQ Global Market (NASDAQ: MNOV) and the Standard Market of the Tokyo Stock Exchange (Code Number: 4875), today provides shareholders a corporate update in the following Letter to
body_text: MediciNova CEO Provides Shareholder Update PDF Version LA JOLLA, Calif., June 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- MediciNova, Inc., a biopharmaceutical company traded on the NASDAQ Global Market (NASDAQ: MNOV) and the Standard Market of the Tokyo Stock Exchange (Code Number: 4875), today provides shareholders a corporate update in the following Letter to Stockholders from CEO Yuichi Iwaki, M.D., Ph.D. Dear Fellow Shareholders, MediciNova continues to make significant progress across its key programs, most recently anchored by the completion of the last patient last visit in our Phase 2 clinical trial of MN-001-NATG-202 evaluating MN-001 (tipelukast) for the treatment of hypertriglyceridemia and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). We anticipate the initial data readout on this trial in third quarter 2026, while continuing to execute on our business plan. Below outlines our progress over the first half of the year, which includes strengthening of our intellectual property portfolio, continued pipeline development, and cultivating relationships in the market to increase our investor awareness. Inclusive of these activities, we attended the annual meeting of BIO2026 in our hometown of San Diego, where we participated in several business development partnering and key networking opportunities. Clinical Development Highlights MN-166 (ibudilast) SEANOBI Study Expanded-Access-Program (EAP) Evaluating MN-166 (ibudilast) in ALS patients: Earlier this year, the Company announced that 12 sites in the U.S. were activated and 100 patients have been enrolled in the SEANOBI study (Scalable Expanded Access with Analysis of Neurofilament and Other Biomarkers in ALS; NCT 06743776) representing 50% of the planned 200-enrollment, evaluating MN-166 (ibudilast) in patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Notice of Allowance for U.S. Patent: The Company received a Notice of Allowance from the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office for a pending patent application that covers the use of ibudilast (MN-166) in combination with an immune checkpoint inhibitor, specifically an anti-PD-1 antibody, for the treatment of glioblastoma. This patent allowance is expected to further strengthen the intellectual property position supporting the Company’s combination therapy development strategy. The patent is expected to expire no earlier than September 2042. The allowed claims cover not only the combination of ibudilast with multiple anti-PD-1 antibodies, but also a broad range of treatment conditions, including duration of administration, dosing frequency, route of administration, dose levels, and dosing schedules. Peer Reviewed Study on Ibudilast Highlighting its Role in Preventing Brain Metastases: Researchers at the Spanish National Cancer Research Centre (CNIO) identified macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF)–mediated reprogramming of CD74-positive microglia and macrophages as a central vulnerability in brain metastasis. The research, recently published in the peer-reviewed journal “ Cancer Research” (March 2026), demonstrates pharmacological modulation of this pathway using the brain-penetrant small molecule ibudilast. The study further demonstrates that ibudilast can effectively block MIF–CD74 signaling, reverse pro-metastatic immune reprogramming, and suppress brain metastasis growth in preclinical systems. MN-001 (tipelukast) Completion of Last Patient Last Visit : The completion of last patient last visit (LPLV) was achieved in its Phase 2 clinical trial, MN-001-NATG-202, evaluating MN-001 (tipelukast) for the treatment of hypertriglyceridemia and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). The MN-001-NATG-202 study is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating MN-001 (tipelukast). Top-line data are expected in the third quarter of 2026. Business and Investor Update A clinical story is only as valuable as the market's ability to see it. Eighteen months ago, one equity research firm covered MediciNova. Today, four do. D. Boral Capital initiated coverage in December 2024 and has continued to publish updates. In 2026, three additional firms initiated: Lucid Capital Markets, with Elmer Piros, Ph.D.; H.C. Wainwright & Co., with Lander Egaña Gorroño, Ph.D.; and Maxim Group, with Jason McCarthy, Ph.D. Four firms now underwrite the science to the Street. For a company of our market capitalization, that is not a routine development. We believe it is a signal that the institutional research community sees the late-stage pipeline, the year-end ALS readout, and the capital-efficient model as worth the desk's time. We welcome the scrutiny. Coverage builds the audience that data will eventually convince. As we move to the second half of 2026, we believe that we have good momentum to continue reaching our milestones, especially an upcoming key catalyst at the end of 2026 related to the topline data for our COMBAT ALS Phase 2b/3 Registration trial, while prudently and carefully managing our finances. We remain committed to helping better the lives of our patients suffering from serious diseases, as well as creating long-term value for our shareholders and we look forward to providing additional updates as they develop. title: Malibu MONSOON Engines: Everything You Ever Wanted to Know
summary: The Malibu Monsoon engine range powers every boat in the lineup. Discover how the M5Di and M6Di deliver class-leading performance, fuel efficiency, and low noise output.
body_text: When you go shopping for a wake boat, it's perfectly normal to get distracted by the flashy paint jobs, onboard gadgets, and interior customization options offered on modern wake boats. But the reality is that the most important component of any wake boat is the engine. Given the critical role an engine plays in your wake boating experience, Malibu Boats proudly mak use of our world-famous MONSOON Engines. The MONSOON series was purpose-designed from the start, to offer reliable, efficient, and quiet performance tailored specifically to the unique demands of wake boats. They are the ultimate representation of everything required of an engine in a next generation wake boat. And we build them right next door to the very same factory building your Malibu boat. Read on to find out how MONSOON engines deliver spectacular wake performance, precise torque control and unforgettable ride experiences, all making it the industry leader in marine engine performance. Built for the Way You Actually Boat Most people don't realize that wake boat engine performance isn't really about top-end horsepower. The thing that really matters is what happens in the first few seconds after you hit the throttle - also known as the 'hole shot'. MONSOON engines are designed specifically for wake sports, prioritizing low-end torque for quick "hole shots" even when boats are fully loaded. An engine's ability to get a fully loaded hull up to surf or wakeboard speed quickly is the true test of its performance, and so that's exactly the challenge the MONSOON M5, M6 and LT4 engines were designed to solve. Efficiency in Wakesurfing Performance When you're out on the water doing watersports, you're living at 3,500 RPM most of the time. Therefore, Malibu engineered MONSOON to hit hard right in that range. MONSOON's torque-focused performance is optimized to peak around 3,500 RPM, making it easier for boats to handle heavy ballast loads. The practical result of this is that the engine isn't working nearly as hard to get the boat moving, which saves fuel. At the same speed, most Malibu boats run at lower RPM than the majority of inboard engines on the water today. This is a meaningful efficiency advantage that translates into lower fuel bills over a full season. Full-spectrum Propeller Performance That strong low-end torque also allows Malibu Boats to run more pitch on the props, which means the MONSOON engine gets you out of the hole (the 'hole shot' we referred to earlier) with authority, and without giving up anything on top-end speed. For most engines, excelling at both ends of the performance spectrum is a genuine engineering challenge. The MONSOON line was purpose-built to live in both worlds. In-House Manufacturing To pull this off, Malibu brought engine production in-house at our state-of-the-art, 70,000 square-foot manufacturing facility in Tennessee. It's there that the team performs research and development on dynos, followed by on-water testing. In fact, we've hit over 5,000 hours of combined testing, and still counting! Custom Gear Ratios Tuned for Your Boat Our engineers calculated custom gear ratios for every single model in the lineup, because a lighter crossover boat and a full-size performance model have genuinely different powertrain needs. Despite weight differences between some models, every boat in the Malibu lineup gets an individually tuned engine setup specifically optimized for its hull. The same thinking applies to our propellers. Malibu tested each of our models from sea level to 8,300 feet of elevation to find optimal propeller pitches for the full lineup. Thanks to these efforts, when you're running at capacity on a high-altitude mountain lake, your MONSOON engine delivers the same performance as it would at sea level. That's not a small thing. Quieter Than You'd Expect. And That Matters More Than You Think Engine noise is one of those things you might not think much about until you've spent a day on a loud boat. By the time you're back at the dock, everyone's a little worn out - not from the sun and the water, but from the constant hum and vibration underfoot. The reason is that engine NVH (noise, vibration, and harshness - a standard industry metric) takes a real personal toll on the overall experience of boating. Independently Tested Quietness For that reason, Malibu invested heavily in making the MONSOON engine line genuinely quiet. Our approach combines strategically placed acoustic foam with the latest direct injection technology, and the results have been independently verified. Testing conducted by Boating Magazine at 3,500 RPM revealed that MONSOON engines registered well below the threshold that can cause hearing damage. Noise: Bad for your Health That might sound like a technical footnote, but consider this: many inboard boats on the water today run at noise levels that, over time, genuinely threaten your hearing health. Malibu's MONSOON engines represent a significant step forward on that front, and that's important because we know that your family is on this boat with you. Beyond the health angle, a quieter engine makes the day better - you can hold a conversation at normal volume, the music on your stereo sounds the way it should, and you arrive back at the dock feeling refreshed rather than wrung out. Inherent Reliability Every MONSOON engine is specifically engineered for absolute reliability at all times, meaning that you never have to worry about whether your MONSOON engine can keep up with your demanding surf lifestyle. That starts with building an engine that is designed from the start, to operate in a marine environment. But taking an automotive engine block and turning it into a reliable marine engine (a process called marinizing) is where many manufacturers run into trouble. Malibu's engineers and partners, however, spent thousands of hours designing, 3D-printing, and testing over 200 custom parts to get this right. The most important of those innovations is built right into the front of the engine -and it changes everything about how our powertrain is designed, serviced, and trusted on the water. Front End Accessory Drive (FeAD) MONSOON's Front-End Accessory Drive (FEAD) is our secret sauce for making the world's greatest wake sports engines. FEAD is a custom-cast, patent-pending accessory system designed to enhance the reliability and serviceability of MONSOON engines. FEAD integrates a cooling system that controls engine oil fluid temperatures, enhancing serviceability and maintenance. The big story about the FeAD system is that it eliminates the automotive water pump and moves critical components - including the alternator, Glycol circulation pump, thermostat housing, and transmission cooler - higher up in the engine where they're easier to service. It also eliminates several failure points that are common in more conventionally marinized engines. The result is that MONSOON engines offer unmatched reliability, easy serviceability, and superior power for surfing and wakeboarding. Closed Cooling System Perhaps the most significant reliability innovation is what Malibu did with cooling. In most marine engines, raw water (water drawn directly from outside the boat) circulates through the engine to keep it cool - but that same raw water brings problems with it. Debris, seaweed, and corrosion can all find their way into cooling passages and cause serious damage. In MONSOON Engines, raw water only touches the exhaust. Everything else, including the engine block, transmission cooler, oil cooler, run in a closed Glycol circuit. Glycol is the same antifreeze compound used in automotive cooling systems and is more efficient than raw water, plus it doesn't carry any of the corrosion or debris risks. It's a fundamentally cleaner, more reliable fully integrated cooling system that delivers stable engine oil fluid temperatures and the kind of reliable engine you would expect from our next generation MONSOON engines. High-precision manufacturing One of the first things we did when building the MONSOON line was to outfit our Tennessee facility with 'smart tools' - systems that show technicians the exact torque specifications for every fastener on a screen, and that won't advance to the next step until the correct torque is achieved with the correct tool. It completely removes human error from the assembly process, granting our manufacturing process a level of precision that compounds across every engine that comes off the line. Industry-Leading Powertrains Wake boats have grown significantly in size, dry weight, and ballast capacity over the years, and the powertrains driving them have had to keep pace. The MONSOON Powertrain Engineering section has a dedicated team that continuously tests combinations of engines, transmissions, props, and programming. The result is a powertrain that leads the wake boat segment in the balance of power, fuel efficiency, and sound emissions. Independent testing conducted by Boating Magazine has also consistently put Malibu's powertrain at the top of the class for fuel economy and sound levels compared to other tow boats. Something else to know is that during their fuel economy testing, Power Wedge® III was not in use. When Power Wedge III's lift mode is engaged in real-world use, it helps the hull get on plane faster, which improves your fuel economy even further. Malibu's leadership extends to MONSOON's factory warranties. MONSOON engines are backed by an industry-best 5-year factory warranty, reflecting massive confidence in their reliability and durability. The Bottom Line The MONSOON M5, M6 and LT4 engines were purpose-built from the ground up for one thing: delivering the best possible experience for wake sports day after day, year after year. The engineering behind them - from their custom gear ratios and prop tuning to the FeAD cooling system and ease of servicing- reflects thousands of hours of testing and refinement, all focused on giving you more time on the water and fewer reasons to think about what's under the hatch. More power where it counts. A quieter ride. Exceptional reliability. Better fuel economy. That's the MONSOON promise - and it's backed by independent data that doesn't lie.

The total incurred net consolidated catastrophe reinsurance premiums ceded to third parties is expected to total $430 - $440 million for the 2026 treaty year. The first event tower, including retentions, is equal to a 1-in-130 year return period, consistent with last year’s program. Market conditions were favorable for this year’s renewal, largely as a result of a healthy reinsurance market, the success of the Florida legislative reforms and the lack of severe storm activity in 2025. Market observers have publicly stated that U.S. property catastrophe cedents are experiencing up to 20% reductions in risk-adjusted pricing, and we believe our renewal is consistent with that market dynamic. The exception is that no risk-adjusted pricing benefit was realized on the $515 million of limit purchased from the Florida Hurricane Catastrophe Fund (“FHCF”) or the $565 million of multi-year bonds issued in 2025. In a four-event hurricane season, our aggregate retention has decreased from $95 million to $75 million. Additionally, our ex-Florida first storm retention decreased from $35 million to $10 million. The $3 billion placement is a combination of protection provided by traditional reinsurers, Insurance Linked Securities (“ILS”) investors, the FHCF and our captive reinsurer. The entire program is indemnity based, with no parametric covers. All reinsurers participating in our 2026-2027 catastrophe reinsurance program were rated A- or better by A.M. Best or were required to post collateral up to 100% of all obligations to the Company. The traditional reinsurance market represents $1.65 billion of limit, up from $1.1 billion last year. The challenge now is making every AI-driven decision controlled, auditable, and ready for the most regulated industry in the world. The performance of banks and insurers hinges on making exceptional customer decisions, and organizations that rapidly adopt AI will race ahead of competitors: Financial institutions that use AI to underwrite businesses in minutes rather than days will sign more customers. Teams that better understand their customers will suffer fewer losses and optimize profitability . Insurers that quickly handle claims with AI will filter out leakage and enhance customer experiences, enabling better combined ratios and lower churn. This is the future we are committed to powering for the benefit of our customers. It’s with this vision in mind that we are excited to announce our $110M Series C fundraise, led by Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives . The successful fundraise opens Taktile’s next chapter, which centers on enabling financial institutions to transform themselves for the AI age. How we’ll empower our customers to meet the moment It is our conviction that the banks and insurers who really break ground with AI transformation won’t be those who automate customer service or marketing. They will be the ones who solve AI deployment where it’s hardest: inside the complex, regulated decisions that drive core business performance. Delivering sustainable production impact from AI in this complex setting requires both industry-specific product capabilities and the team to deliver the transformation. Our Series C funding gives us the resources to build out both. We’re investing in our highly successful forward-deployed engineering team—a team that has proven it can help banks and insurers deliver millions of dollars of impact in real production scenarios. Already, one of the world’s largest insurers is running multiple use cases on Taktile, with projected cost efficiencies of more than $90M in claims processing alone. With our product roadmap, we’re focused on creating a reality where AI not only changes our customers’ businesses, but also reshapes how value gets delivered: In the future, our customers will just say what they want to build on Taktile rather than configuring it themselves. Even the most complex interactions with the platform will be done through natural language. Taktile AI will not only help financial institutions make better customer decisions, it will proactively monitor these decisions and improve itself. Humans using Taktile will continue to play a critical role, but their job will shift from repetitive tasks to managing the agentic workforce, ensuring that every decision made is the best one for the business. title: Digital Front Door for Hospitals: How to Connect Your Website, WhatsApp, Messenger, Viber, LINE, and SMS
summary: Build a digital front door across every channel patients use.
body_text: Summary A digital front door for a hospital is the set of channels patients use to first interact with the hospital — typically the website, WhatsApp, Messenger, Viber, LINE, Telegram, SMS, and call center — unified so patients get a consistent, instant, and clinically safe experience regardless of where they start. AI Agents make a digital front door practical at hospital scale. They handle the bulk of repetitive patient interactions across channels while escalating clinical, sensitive, and complex cases to the right human team. What does "digital front door" mean? Originally a US healthcare concept, the digital front door describes how patients enter the healthcare system in the digital era. It includes: The hospital website Patient portals Online booking Chat apps (WhatsApp, Messenger, Viber, LINE, Telegram) SMS Email Voice / call center A good digital front door is not just a list of channels. It is: Consistent across channels Always-on Multilingual Integrated with the EMR Safe — with escalation to humans when needed Why hospitals need a digital front door Patients no longer wait for office hours to interact with a hospital. They expect: Instant answers Easy booking Convenient reminders Personalized follow-up In the language and channel they prefer A traditional call center cannot scale to meet that expectation. A modern digital front door — anchored by AI Agents — can. For hospitals, the benefits include: Higher inquiry-to-booking conversion Lower call-center costs Better marketing attribution Improved patient satisfaction Cleaner data flowing into the EMR 24/7 availability without 24/7 staffing Digital front door for hospitals: key points A digital front door spans web, chat apps, SMS, and call center. AI Agents make it scalable. It must be unified — one patient profile, one set of workflows, one analytics view. It must integrate with the EMR, HIS, CRM, scheduling, and quality systems. It must support multilingual patient populations. It must include human handover for clinical or sensitive cases. It is governed by healthcare compliance, audit trails, and security controls. It is most often built in phases — channel by channel, workflow by workflow. The components of a digital front door Website with embedded chat The hospital website is the entry point for organic search, paid ads, and direct visitors. An embedded chat widget lets patients ask questions, get recommendations, and book appointments without leaving the site. Chat apps WhatsApp, Messenger, Viber, LINE, and Telegram cover most patient populations across Asia-Pacific. Each channel runs the same AI Agent workflows. See our omnichannel guide . SMS The universal fallback. Useful for older patient cohorts and as a backup channel when chat-app reach is low. Call center For complex cases, sensitive conversations, and escalations. AI Agents deflect repetitive volume so the call center can focus on the work that needs humans. Patient profile Unified across channels. A patient who starts on the website should be able to continue on WhatsApp without losing context. Care team dashboard A unified inbox where staff handle escalations from every channel. One workflow, not seven. What AI Agents do in the digital front door A complete digital front door uses several AI Agents: FAQ Agent — answers common questions, deflects from call center Recommendation Agent — matches patient to specialist or service Scheduling Agent — books, confirms, reschedules Pre-Admission Agent — collects forms and consent Patient Education Agent — prepares patients for visits Remote Monitoring Agent — tracks recovery after visits Marketing Conversion Agent — re-engages patients who drop off Patient Survey Agent — collects experience and outcome data Example workflow: From organic search to recovered drop-off Patient searches "cataract surgery cost" on Google Lands on the hospital website Chat widget opens with the FAQ Agent ready to answer Patient asks about pricing — gets accurate, current information Recommendation Agent suggests the right ophthalmology package Patient hesitates — closes the browser tab without booking Marketing Conversion Agent sends a follow-up message via WhatsApp 24 hours later Patient comes back and books the appointment Reminders, pre-admission, education, and surveys all flow through Bot MD How to build a digital front door Pick a starting channel — usually WhatsApp or your website Pick a starting workflow — usually appointment booking or FAQ deflection Integrate with the EMR or scheduling system Pilot for 30–90 days, measure Add channels — WhatsApp → Messenger → Viber → LINE → SMS → Web Add agents — FAQ → Scheduling → Pre-Admission → Education → Monitoring → Surveys → Marketing Unify the patient profile across channels Train staff on the unified inbox and escalation workflows What patients experience Patients don't see "the digital front door." They see: A hospital that answers them instantly, in their language A hospital that lets them book without calling A hospital that remembers them across channels A hospital that follows up after their visit A hospital that reaches a human when they need one The digital front door is invisible — and that's the point. What hospital teams can automate Marketing teams Multi-channel patient acquisition with full attribution from ad to booking to attendance. Patient experience teams Consistent patient experience across channels. Fewer complaints. Higher CSAT. Operations teams Cleaner data in the EMR. Less manual reconciliation. Better visibility. Clinical teams Less time spent on logistics; more time on care. IT teams One platform to integrate, secure, and maintain — not seven. Integration requirements A digital front door integrates with: EMR / HIS — for appointments, patient records, intake Scheduling system — for live availability CRM — for campaigns and patient profile Payment gateway — for deposits and fees Quality Management System — for surveys and reporting Care team dashboards — for escalations Knowledge base / CMS — for FAQ accuracy See How Healthcare Systems Can Integrate with WhatsApp for technical detail and our integrations page for supported partners. Safety and human handover A safe digital front door includes: Clinical escalation rules Human handover at any point Audit trails for every interaction RBAC and SSO for staff access Consent capture where required Multilingual fail-safes Healthcare-grade compliance (ISO 27001 / 27017 / 27018 / SOC 2) Data residency options See our Security & Compliance posture. What to look for in a digital front door platform Capability Why it matters Omnichannel coverage Patients use different channels Unified patient profile Continuous conversation across channels Healthcare-specific AI Agents Built for clinical workflows EMR / scheduling integration Real-time, two-way Multilingual Across your patient population Human handover Clinical and sensitive cases escalate to humans Unified staff inbox One workflow, not one per channel Audit trails Every interaction logged Compliance ISO 27001 / SOC 2 / local privacy Deployment options Cloud, on-prem, hospital server How Bot MD helps build a digital front door Bot MD provides the AI Agent layer for a hospital digital front door. Eight healthcare-specific AI Agents , omnichannel coverage (WhatsApp, Messenger, Viber, LINE, Telegram, SMS, Web), EMR / HIS / CRM / scheduling integration, and healthcare-grade compliance — all out of the box. Bot MD is in production across 60+ hospital and clinic networks supporting 300,000+ patients across Asia-Pacific. Example result: $300K in recovered appointment revenue One tertiary private hospital used Bot MD's Marketing Conversion Agent for missed-appointment recovery and generated $300K in recovered revenue from a single campaign. See our case studies . Build a digital front door without replacing your team. Bot MD’s AI Agents power a hospital digital front door across web, WhatsApp, Messenger, Viber, LINE, Telegram, and SMS — integrated with your EMR, with full audit and human handover. See the AI Agent suite FAQ Do we need to replace our website? No. Bot MD integrates with your existing website via an embedded chat widget. No replatforming required. What about our call center? The call center stays — for complex cases. AI Agents deflect repetitive volume, freeing the call center for the work that needs humans. How do we measure ROI? Common metrics: inquiry-to-booking conversion, no-show rate, call-center deflection, patient satisfaction, recovered revenue. How long does deployment take? A focused use case ships in weeks. A full digital front door rollout is typically a 6–12 month program with phased channels and agents. Do we need every channel? No. Start with the channel your patients use most. Add others as demand grows. What about compliance? A healthcare-specific platform handles compliance uniformly across channels. ISO 27001, 27017, 27018, and SOC 2 certifications are table stakes for hospital deployments. What's the right starting point? Most hospitals start with WhatsApp + appointment booking. It's high-volume, has clear ROI, and exercises the integrations you'll need everywhere else. How do we handle staff training? Bot MD provides a unified staff inbox that consolidates escalations from every channel. Staff training is one workflow, not one per channel. Can we use multiple AI Agent platforms? Most hospitals consolidate on one. Running multiple platforms creates data fragmentation, compliance complexity, and confusing patient experiences. Does the digital front door include voice / call center? The AI Agent layer handles digital channels. Your existing call center continues to handle phone calls. Both can write to the same EMR. What's the difference between a digital front door and a chatbot? A chatbot answers questions on one channel. A digital front door is the full patient access strategy — across channels, anchored by AI Agents, integrated with hospital systems, and unified with the call center.

title: Common SBA Loan Mistakes That Delay Approval – And How To Avoid Them
summary: Avoid common SBA loan mistakes that can delay approval. Learn how to streamline your application and move forward with confidence.
body_text: Summary Securing a Small Business Administration (SBA) loan doesn’t have to be complicated but small missteps can slow down the process. From incomplete documentation and unclear financials to delayed communication and choosing the wrong loan structure, many common challenges are avoidable with the right preparation. By understanding what lenders are looking for and working with the right partner early, business owners can streamline the SBA loan process and avoid unnecessary delays so they can stay focused on achieving their growth goals. How to Avoid Delays in the SBA Loan Process Running a business takes imagination, determination and – let’s be honest – a fair amount of capital. A Small Business Administration (SBA) loan can be a powerful way to fuel growth, whether you’re expanding operations (like opening a second location), acquiring a business or investing in new equipment (maybe you need to upgrade outdated technology or purchase company vehicles to support demand). But while SBA financing can open the door to new opportunities, the process can sometimes feel complex to potential borrowers and small missteps can lead to unnecessary delays. The good news? Most delays are avoidable with the right preparation and a clear understanding of what lenders are looking for. Before you apply, it’s worth taking a look at common SBA loan mistakes so you can move forward with confidence from the start. 1. Lack of Organization or Preparation Applying for an SBA loan is not something you want to rush. Many business owners underestimate how much information is required or wait until funding is urgent (like realizing you need financing only after signing a lease for a new space). This lack of preparation often leads to disorganized submissions, missing documents and shifting plans, all of which slow down the approval process. How to avoid it: Start the SBA loan process well before you need funding. Create a checklist of required documents and milestones. Keep your business and financial records organized year-round. 2. Not Understanding SBA Loan Eligibility Requirements Before your SBA loan application is even reviewed, your business must meet baseline criteria. Typically, businesses must be for-profit, operate in the U.S., meet size standards and demonstrate the ability to repay the loan. Skipping this step can lead to immediate delays, or even a denial. How to avoid it: Confirm your SBA loan eligibility before applying. Be prepared to demonstrate consistent revenue and business stability. Clearly define how the loan will support your business goals. Remember, meeting the minimum requirements is just the starting point. Lenders will still evaluate your financial strength and overall risk profile. 3. Involving Your SBA lender Too Late in the Process It’s easy to think of a lender as the final step but bringing them in late can actually slow things down. By the time an application is complete, key decisions about structure, documentation or eligibility may already need to be revised. Involving an SBA lender earlier in the process can help you avoid missteps before they ever happen. From shaping your loan request to identifying potential challenges, early guidance often leads to a faster, more efficient experience overall. How to avoid it: Connect with an SBA lender early in the process. Ask questions early to ensure your approach aligns with SBA expectations. Leverage your lender’s expertise to strengthen your application from the beginning. When you treat your lender as a partner, not just a checkpoint, you’re setting your application up for success from day one. 4. Choosing the Wrong Loan Structure or Lender Not all SBA loans or lenders are the same. Applying for a program that doesn’t fit your needs or partnering with a lender who is not aligned with your business can introduce unnecessary friction and slow things down. Each SBA loan program is designed for a specific purpose, so choosing the wrong one may require adjustments mid-process. Similarly, a lender without experience in your industry may need additional time to fully understand your business and financing needs. How to avoid it: Understand the difference between SBA loan programs. Choose a lender with experience in your industry. Look for a partner who can guide you, not just process paperwork. The right combination of loan structure and lender doesn’t just improve your odds of approval; it can make the entire experience smoother from start to finish. 5. Submitting Incomplete or Inaccurate Information One of the biggest causes of delays is simple: missing or inconsistent documentation. SBA loan applications require detailed financial records, including tax returns, profit and loss statements and business plans. When documents are incomplete, or don’t match, lenders often need to pause the process and request clarification. How to avoid it: Prepare documents early and keep them up to date. Double-check for accuracy and consistency across all forms. Work with a trusted advisor or SBA lender to review your application. A well-prepared application doesn’t just save time. It signals to lenders that your business is organized and ready for financing. 6. Weak Financial Story (Cash Flow, Credit and Projections) Your financials tell the story of your business, and lenders are paying close attention. Issues like inconsistent cash flow, unrealistic projections or unaddressed credit problems can raise red flags and slow down the approval process. Think of your financials as more than just numbers. They’re your opportunity to show how your business performs today and where it’s headed next. If that story feels incomplete or unclear, lenders may need additional time to dig deeper and ask questions. How to avoid it: Ensure your financial projections are realistic and backed by data. Review and strengthen your credit profile before applying. Clearly demonstrate how your business will repay the loan. The goal isn’t perfection. It’s clarity and credibility in your financial history. 7. Poor or Delayed Communication Even a strong application can stall if communication breaks down. Responding slowly to lender requests or missing key follow-ups can delay underwriting, especially since lenders are often reviewing multiple applications at once. How to avoid it: Respond promptly to all requests for information. Keep communication clear and consistent. Work with a lender who values transparency and responsiveness. A smooth process isn’t just about paperwork. It’s about staying engaged every step of the way. Move Forward with Confidence An SBA loan should accelerate your business, not hold it back. With the right preparation and partner, you can avoid delays and move with confidence. At First Internet Bank, we make it simpler, faster and more aligned to your goals. Take the next step and see what’s possible. Learn more about SBA loans and start imagining what’s next for your business.
